standard_prerequisites: The approximation theorem for objects of the derived category by perfect complexes, cited from the same chapter
Ext vanishing for cones with truncated cohomology support, and the presentation of pseudo-coherent objects as homotopy colimits of perfect objects
Duality for perfect complexes on ringed sites and preservation of perfectness under derived tensor and pushforward
core_obligations: Part (A): reduce to E perfect via an approximation P to E of amplitude tuned to a and m, control kernel and cokernel of the induced Ext map through the cone C, and invoke the perfect case
Part (B): write E as a homotopy colimit of perfect E_n, form the inverse system K_n of pushed-forward duals, and show the transition maps on Ext are isomorphisms in a growing degree range
Deduce that the dual system L_n has transition maps isomorphic on truncations tau_{>= -n-a+2}, hence L = hocolim L_n is pseudo-coherent
Conclude by the mapping property of homotopy colimits that Ext against L computes the target Ext groups in the stable range
proof_roadmap: Shrink to a Noetherian X around the supports of the flat complex
For (A): approximate E by perfect P, compare Ext groups through the cone, and quote the perfect case with its boundary statement
For (B): build the inverse system K_n from duals of the perfect approximations and check the degree ranges of the isomorphisms
Dualize to a direct system L_n, verify truncation isomorphisms via the last nonvanishing cohomology of the cone, and finish with the homotopy colimit mapping property
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is a two-part representation theorem for Ext groups against a bounded flat complex with proper support: first by cohomology of a perfect object of the base, then by a pseudo-coherent object dual to a homotopy colimit construction (source lines 6009-6131, label lemma-compute-ext). The solver must run an approximation-and-cone reduction with explicit degree bookkeeping, then an inverse/direct system argument whose truncation isomorphisms come from the last nonvanishing cohomology sheaf of a cone; neither half is a routine citation. Allowed background: the chapter's approximation theorem, pseudo-coherent hocolim lemma and dual perfect complex machinery, delivered as navigation pointers.
